clue.text: Hollywood. Mrs White presumably for Buttons?

definitions.text: Hollywood. Mrs White presumably for Buttons?

parts.words: Hollywood. Mrs White presumably for Buttons?
parts.note: Pearl White was a Hollywood silent-film star, so her mum would be the parent of that actress; buttons are often made from the shiny lining of oyster shells

explanation.surface: A query about a film star's mother and what she might use to fasten clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearl White starred in the silent serial The Perils of Pauline; the iridescent shell lining used for buttons carries the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The nacre lining oyster shells, a classic button material, shares its name with the parent of the actress Pearl.

clue.text: False report heard of girl flying with Red Arrows?

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase that follows is spoken and we write down what it sounds like

parts.note: a Miss flying alongside the RAF display team would be a miss in formation

explanation.surface: Someone spreads an untrue rumour about a young woman flying with the RAF display team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Arrows are the RAF aerobatic display team, famous for close formation flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue news put about is wrong information, a false report.

clue.text: Take a trip out to the zoo to find him

indicators.note: out describes the letters of the words as disordered, sent away from their usual arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to an outing at the zoo to look for a particular animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles A TRIP into the animal; the zoo context makes 'him' the animal you would go there to see.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for a beast seen at the zoo, here the snouted South American mammal.

clue.text: Like returning astronauts, or those who never went

definitions.meaning: space travellers coming home are heading for the planet's surface
people who never left the ground are stuck on the planet

explanation.surface: Contrasts spacemen coming home with people who never left the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading back toward our planet, or confined to it and never airborne: both senses of the compound adjective.

clue.text: Position right for military leader

parts.note: an office is a post or position held

explanation.surface: A job description: the correct posting for someone commanding troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissioned army officer holds rank and leads soldiers.

clue.text: Select feller needed to break the ice

parts.note: to pick is to select
an axe fells trees, so it is a feller

explanation.surface: Choosing the right tool for smashing through ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like slang for a chap; it is a tree-cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed digging tool is used to split hard surfaces such as ice.

clue.text: Objects to good writing?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone protests against fine prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a verb (protests) but is the plural noun meaning goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects in the sense of goals or targets are what one strives toward.

clue.text: Car minus oil — engine-head needs replacing

indicators.note: the letters must be put back in a new order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the head of engine is its first letter E

explanation.surface: A motorist's complaint: no oil, and the cylinder head must be swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs replacing' rearranges MINUS OIL into LIMOUSIN, then the E from the head of 'engine' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A large luxurious chauffeur-driven saloon is a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Warm up her cough medicine, that's material

parts.note: to heat is to warm up
taken as written
a cough mixture is a liquid medicine

explanation.surface: Instructions to heat a woman's cough syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a speckled tweed fabric, its colours said to resemble moorland plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A flecked woollen tweed is a type of cloth or fabric.

clue.text: In charge proof is oddly put as means of getting off

indicators.note: letters set down in a strange way signal a rearrangement of the words

explanation.surface: Someone in authority finds that the evidence has been presented strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly put' rearranges PROOF IS into SOPORIF, then IC follows. 'getting off' is getting off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleep-inducing drug helps a person drop off into slumber.

clue.text: Name of the friend seen with Monsieur

parts.note: amie is French for a female friend

explanation.surface: Asking who the companion is who accompanies a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monsieur' signals both the French abbreviation M and the French word for a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's first name, borne for instance by the wife of President Eisenhower.

clue.text: Lord of Eden End?

parts.note: Lord Frederick was a British prime minister like Eden, and the word also names a compass end, the top of the map

explanation.surface: Who is the aristocrat presiding over Priestley's play Eden End?
explanation.walkthrough: Eden End is a J B Priestley play; Lord North was an 18th-century prime minister, as Anthony Eden was a 20th-century one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was prime minister, as Eden was, and the word is also a compass point or end.

clue.text: Not the boatman's favourite catch

parts.note: rowers who mistime a stroke and trap the oar blade under water are said to catch one of these shellfish

explanation.surface: A fisherman's least favourite haul.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, catching a crab means fouling the stroke, which can throw the rower off the seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing blunder is named after the shellfish one is said to catch.

clue.text: Case of diamonds ?

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit is a legal case
diamonds is one of the four card groups in a pack

explanation.surface: Something to hold precious gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action brought in court, and one of the four card families such as diamonds.

clue.text: The Criterion for As You Like It?

definitions.meaning: a standard or test by which things are judged
the court jester in Shakespeare's comedy

explanation.surface: Naming the yardstick by which a Shakespeare comedy is judged.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C and italics suggest the Criterion Theatre in London staging the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A test stone for gold gives a standard of judgement, and the jester in Shakespeare's Arden comedy bears the name.

clue.text: Excel, getting gold in such sports

parts.note: to outdo others is to excel
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An athlete shines and takes a gold medal in a type of game.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the adjective describing sports played in the open air, so 'such sports' means sports of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Games played in the open air rather than indoors are of this kind.

clue.text: Henry found Thomas uncommonly blunt and true

indicators.note: uncommonly says the letters appear in an unusual order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A king judged Thomas to be outspoken and honest.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry II called Thomas Becket 'this turbulent priest'; 'uncommonly' rearranges BLUNT and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry II famously complained of the troublesome priest Becket, so the king found Thomas unruly and stormy.

clue.text: Poet's black tie ruined by vulcanized rubber

parts.note: ebon is a poetic word for black

indicators.note: ruined says the word tie is wrecked and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet's dark necktie spoiled by hardened rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns TIE into ITE after EBON.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard black vulcanite is a type of rubber hardened with sulphur.

clue.text: Soldiers at home breaking horses

indicators.note: breaking says one piece forces its way into the middle of another

parts.note: mares are female horses
in means at home

explanation.surface: Troops based locally are training horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking horses' suggests training them; here IN breaks into MARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-going soldiers of a navy's infantry corps.

clue.text: Position for a trainer

definitions.meaning: a post or place where someone is ...
a train-er, something for trains, is a railway stop

explanation.surface: Where a coach should stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A post one is assigned, and the halt where trains call.

clue.text: Heard request to identify tree

indicators.note: heard says the phrase is spoken aloud and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: asking which elm one means is a request to identify a tree

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a question asking what a tree is.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken question 'which elm?' asks which tree is meant; it sounds like the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-leaved European species of the Ulmus family.

clue.text: House official has a favourite dog

parts.note: a whip is a party official in the House of Commons who enforces voting
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A parliamentarian owns a beloved hound.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip in Parliament keeps party members voting the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender racing breed resembling a small greyhound.

clue.text: Among leaders of the hooligans using garotte

definitions.text: Among leaders of the hooligans using garotte

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Ringleaders of a gang strangle victims with a cord.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'the hooligans using garotte' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian; historically an Indian strangler who used a cord.

clue.text: In King's square a student of Hindu divinity

indicators.note: In places the following pieces inside the chess square

parts.note: in old descriptive chess notation K1 is the King's square, with 1 read as I
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A scholar of Hindu religion stands in a royal square.
explanation.walkthrough: Descriptive chess notation names squares by piece, so K1 is the king's starting square; read the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu goddess of destruction, a consort of Shiva, is a deity.

clue.text: Making fifty, with a six, shows the class of the willow

indicators.note: with here means holding, so the six encloses the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A batsman reaches a half-century with a big hit, showing the quality of his bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket bats are made of willow, so the surface praises a batsman; the answer is the willow genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus name of willow trees.

clue.text: Painter shows end of Brutus's last battle

indicators.note: end of means only the closing part is kept, the front letters dropped

parts.note: Brutus was defeated and died at Philippi in 42 BC

explanation.surface: An artist depicts the final clash of Caesar's assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' keeps the end of PHILIPPI, dropping PHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra Filippo and his son Filippino were Florentine Renaissance artists of this name.

clue.text: Poison, precious to Milton and to Mrs Webb

definitions.meaning: something deadly, as in the plant name wolfsbane

definitions.text: precious to Milton and to Mrs Webb
definitions.meaning: Milton wrote 'precious ...' in Paradise Lost and Mary Webb took the phrase as her novel's title

explanation.surface: A toxin that a poet and a novelist both treasured.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly toxin, and the word coupled with 'precious' by Milton and by Mary Webb for her novel.

clue.text: Ring, by a writer of this

definitions.text: Ring, by a writer of this

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle, composed by a master of the musical stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Ring is a cycle of these works, so the whole clue also points to the art form.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring cycle is staged music drama, written by a composer of such works.

clue.text: Not the performance expected from the B-P boys

definitions.text: Not the performance expected from the B-P boys

parts.words: Not the performance expected from the B-P boys
parts.note: Baden-Powell's Scouts have the motto Be Prepared, so an unrehearsed show is not what they would give

explanation.surface: The Scouts' show disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: B-P is Robert Baden-Powell, founder of the Scouts, whose motto is Be Prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrehearsed, off-the-cuff performance is the opposite of being prepared.

clue.text: Being obedient in courtly service

definitions.meaning: a tennis server on court must keep their feet at the baseline

explanation.surface: A courtier behaves submissively in royal attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeying the rules, and literally keeping the feet at the baseline when serving on a tennis court.
